text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called on government departments and agencies to ensure that no-one in Vietnam goes hungry during the coming lunar new year festivities.
-- Vietnam expects to welcome 1.9 million foreign travellers in 1997, according to the National Administration for Tourism.
-- Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung is visiting the United States to promote dialogue and trade ties.

-- The National Assembly's Standing Committee has called for basic amendments to the Penal Code. Temporary penalties for corruption and drug offences have been submitted to the National assembly pending formal changes to the law.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for writers to visit construction projects to gain experience and material for their literary works.
-- The latest round of border talks between Vietnam and China ended in Beijing in an atmosphere of friendship and frankness. The next round is scheduled to take place in Vietnam.
-- Hanoi People's Committee Chairman Hoang Van Nghien has pledged that the city authorities will increase efforts to help the Hanoi Police force maintain social order.

- - - - NOTE: Vietnam is celebrating the Tet lunar new year festival from February 6 to 10 and most newspapers are closed during all or part of this period. The daily press digest will therefore resume after the holiday on February 11.
